- Model consistently underestimates prices in early days of the 30-day forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–7 days.
- Overshoots occur after sharp price spikes in the history (e.g., after 94.51 or 93.62), leading to overprediction of subsequent values.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: forecasts tend to revert to lower levels after recent high prices, but often overshoots the true mean.
- Forecast lag: model lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in downward trends.
- Model overreacts to recent low prices, producing overly pessimistic forecasts when prices are recovering.
- Forecasts are too conservative in the final 5–7 days of the 30-day window, underestimating rebound potential.
- Model fails to capture momentum in price trends — especially when history shows accelerating or decelerating trends.
- Forecasts are overly smooth; fail to reflect volatility clustering or sudden reversals in the last 5–10 days of history.
